rule: Terraform Enterprise releases.json uses calendar versions (vYYYYMM-N) and can lag the deck's 2026 semver entries; verify TFE source freshness and never downgrade slide 8 to older data
When Vault release highlights are unavailable, leave slides 11/12 unchanged and flag for manual highlight entry; never pair new versions with stale/blank highlights

Vault changelog_url must point to the PUBLIC hashicorp/vault main CHANGELOG (blob/main/CHANGELOG.md); the releases API url_changelog points at the private vault-enterprise repo and per-version public tags don't all exist. Agent fetches the consolidated changelog once and greps the '## <version>' section for each highlight.

HCP Vault (slide 12) tracks the same Vault core versions as Vault Enterprise (slide 11); when 11 gains a new June release and 12 has no June column, flag 12 for manual structural update rather than silently shipping it a release behind

Reviewer: diff a:t text via XML DOM (getElementsByTagName('a:t')), not a <a:t>...</a:t> regex; deck-wide xml:space=preserve repairs and <a:tab> elements cause false text-diff positives on out-of-scope slides

Release slides (7,8,11,12) are a ROLLING 3-column window driven by products.<product>.latest in releases.json, NOT a full rewrite. Each column is a (month-header, entry) pair; col3 is always the latest. Rule: if latest.month_label == current col3 header month, refresh col3's entry in place and leave col1/col2 untouched; if latest's month is newer, shift the (header,entry) pairs one column left (col1<-col2, col2<-col3, oldest drops) and write latest into col3. NEVER blank or rebuild all 3 columns from the API (it caps at 20 items; for Vault all same-month backports, so col1/col2 history can't be re-derived and must be preserved). Slides 11 (Vault Ent) and 12 (HCP Vault) use the same vault.latest but apply the rule independently against their own columns (12 may lag) — goal is neither stays a month behind; they need NOT be byte-identical. The build reads data/slide-structure.json (from scripts/map_slides.py, regenerated each run in run.sh Phase 2b) for exact shape roles/geometry so it never re-discovers layout.

Deterministic slide geometry: scripts/map_slides.py extracts each automatable slide's editable shapes (role, x/y, text, hyperlinks) into data/slide-structure.json. run.sh Phase 2b regenerates it against the fresh working copy. Agents (esp. pptx-orchestrator) MUST consume it instead of dumping geometry themselves — this was the biggest time/quota sink.

RETRACTED (was 'COLUMN BLOAT FAILURE', run 1558 — diagnosis WRONG). The original deck's release columns are HAND-CURATED and already hold a VARIABLE number of version entries (original: slide 7 col2/May=5 patches, col1/April=2; slide 11 col1 March/April=3 incl v2.0.0+sub-bullets). The build did NOT bloat: it preserved col1/col2 verbatim and only refreshed col3 with products.<product>.latest. CORRECT STANDARD: a column may hold 1+ entries; never collapse a multi-entry column; refresh col3 (or shift on a new month) and leave col1/col2 byte-identical. recent_count is irrelevant to the build (renders latest).

Verify the hide step via <p:sld ... show="0"> on each SLIDE-ROOT file (ppt/slides/slideN.xml), resolving display position->file with `python scripts/hide_slides.py UNPACKED --list`. Do NOT count `show` on <p:sldId> in ppt/presentation.xml — PowerPoint 'Hide Slide' sets it on the slide root, so presentation.xml checks give a FALSE 'zero hidden' (bogus FAIL on run 1558, whose 10/14/18-22 WERE hidden). A hidden slide RETAINS its text, so past-dated text in slideN.xml is NOT evidence the slide is visible — check show.

When events.json status == 'unavailable' (e.g. HTTP 429, not a confirmed-empty fetch), pick ONE policy and make build notes match the deck: either hide event slides 10/14/18-22 (show="0") or leave them unchanged — but never ship past-dated (< today) webinars/events as visible.

Deterministic post-build verification: scripts/verify_deck.py machine-checks the produced deck (integrity/slide-count vs original, hide audit via on slide ROOTS, style_check, and that each release slide's latest/col3 column carries products.

.latest.version). run.sh Phase 4b runs it before the AI reviewer and writes output/verify-*.txt, which the reviewer reads as ground truth instead of eyeballing XML. This replaces ad-hoc manual XML checks and prevents the two mistakes seen on run 1558: the reviewer's false hide-FAIL (it checked presentation.xml) and a human mis-reading variable-entry columns as 'bloat'. The verifier also prints entries-per-column so the hand-curated multi-entry layout is self-evident.

Release-column version runs can SHARE one hyperlink rId with another entry: slide 11 col3 v2.0.2 and col2 v2.0.1 both use rId6 -> tag/v2.0.1, so the v2.0.2 'tag' link actually points at v2.0.1 (pre-existing in the source deck). Verify each version run's hlinkClick rId resolves to ITS OWN vX.Y.Z tag; when refreshing/adding an entry, give it its own rel rather than reusing a shared one (the build correctly minted rId8->v2.0.3).

Blog slides may carry pre-existing entries BELOW the refreshed newest-first top list that are not in blogs.json and may sit out of strict date order (slide 13 'June 4 - Rethinking infrastructure access' renders under May entries). The build only refreshes the top of the list from blogs.json; do not flag these lower curated/out-of-order entries as build errors.

A release's authoritative identity is its DATE, not the printed version string: original decks can mislabel a version (e.g. slide 7 showed '1.15.4 (2026-05-27)' but that date is really 1.15.5, and even its hyperlink pointed at v1.15.5). Reconcile every dated entry against releases.json keyed by exact date; the API data wins, the hyperlink is corroborating-only (never the sole basis for a change). This is now enforced deterministically by scripts/edit_release_slides.py (reconcile pass) and guarded by scripts/verify_deck.py Check 5 (release_accuracy).

Release slides 7,8,11,12 are edited deterministically by scripts/edit_release_slides.py BEFORE the build agent; it writes data/release-edit-report.json with fallback_slides[] (ambiguous, agent handles) and handled_slides[] (done, agent must not re-touch). When fixing a release-slide hyperlink, mint a FRESH relationship id (rIds are often SHARED across entries — mutating a shared rel's Target corrupts a sibling entry's link).

The HashiCorp events page (hashicorp.com/en/events) is behind a Vercel Security Checkpoint (JS challenge) that 429s BOTH plain HTTP and the agent's web_fetch. The reliable fix is a headless Chromium (Playwright): it executes the challenge JS, gets the clearance cookie, and the real page renders (title 'HashiCorp Events'). scripts/fetch_events.py now does this deterministically. Event cards are line-structured text: line0='MON D, YYYY' date, line1=TYPE (WEBINAR/CONFERENCE), line2=title, then product tags (Terraform/Vault/...). Bucket webinars by PRODUCT TAG (reliable), not title keywords; CONFERENCE/in-person -> featured. The sitemap (hashicorp.com/sitemap.xml) IS reachable but lists event URLs without dates, so it can't drive 'upcoming'. Python writes the facts (date/title/url/products); the deck-data agent only fills description/location prose and must NOT change facts when status=='ok'.

When refreshing/replacing a release-entry paragraph (e.g. col3 latest), also clear or repoint any stale <a:hlinkClick> left inside that paragraph's <a:endParaRPr> — it is non-visible cruft (slide 7 v1.15.6's endParaRPr still pointed rId6->v1.15.5) that makes link audits chase a phantom second target. Verify hyperlinks per VISIBLE a:r run, not per-paragraph aggregate.

Featured slide 22 locale fallback: the slide-map marks it French (Paris) and says keep locale if reused, but when events.json has NO upcoming French event it is acceptable to reuse slide 22 for the next-soonest English featured event (keeps the slot productive) rather than hiding it — provided the locale switch is noted in build notes.

Blog slides 9 (Terraform) and 13 (Vault) are now edited DETERMINISTICALLY by scripts/edit_blog_slides.py (run.sh Phase 3c) BEFORE the build agent. It refreshes the top N = len(blogs.products.<product>.recent) entries: rewrites the date run (preserving leading whitespace + ' – ' separator, formatting the date as full-month '%B %-d' e.g. 'June 16'), collapses the full post title into the first title run (removing surplus title runs — Google-Slides export bold splitting is noise, not semantic), and repoints the 'See here' hyperlink via a FRESH rel (shared rIds are never mutated). Older entries below the top N are left as history. The build agent must NOT touch slides 9/13. Guarded by verify_deck Check 6 (blog_coverage).

Event slides are now edited DETERMINISTICALLY by scripts/edit_event_slides.py (run.sh Phase 3d) BEFORE the build agent: webinar slots (10,14) and featured (18-22). Slots are filled in READING ORDER (sort by rounded-y then x) with events sorted SOONEST-upcoming-first (ascending date) — this is the agreed ordering for 'upcoming' slides (matches what a human expects and the prior agent's featured output); slide-map fill is now 'soonest_first'. Webinar slot p0 = '<DATE upper> | WEBINAR | ' + 'See here'(link); p1 = title; p2+ description bullets collapse to the single events.json sentence (delete surplus <a:p>). Surplus slots are cleared to a single empty '<a:p><a:endParaRPr lang=en-US/></a:p>'; a product with zero webinars HIDES the slide (show='0'). Featured: Title 1=title, Subtitle 2='Event | <display_date> | '+'Register Here'(link), Content Placeholder 4=description (collapse to 1 para); slides past the supply are HIDDEN. All hyperlinks use FRESH rels (slide 14 slots SHARE rId4 in the source deck — mutating it would corrupt siblings). The build agent must NOT touch 10/14/18-22. Guarded by verify_deck Check 7 (event_coverage).

Blog refresh must de-duplicate the newly-written top-N posts against the preserved tail entries on the SAME slide: if a refreshed newest-first post equals a curated lower entry (slide 13: 'SCIM in HashiCorp Vault standardizes provisioning in platforms', May 28), drop/replace the duplicate so the same blog is not shown twice. Distinct from the out-of-order-tail rule (which is acceptable).

When removing or replacing a linked release entry (e.g. swapping a pre-release col3 entry for a stable one), also PRUNE the now-orphaned <Relationship> from ppt/slides/slideN.xml.rels. clean.py removes unreferenced media but NOT unreferenced hyperlink rels: slide 7 left rId11 -> v1.16.0-alpha20260603 fully orphaned after v1.15.6 replaced the alpha. Harmless but makes link audits chase phantom targets.

Blog top-N refresh can DUPLICATE a post: the feed window (blogs.json recent[]) overlaps the deck's curated history, so a refreshed top-N entry can equal a preserved lower 'tail' entry (e.g. slide 13 showed 'SCIM ... May 28' twice). edit_blog_slides.py now DE-DUPS: after refreshing the top N, it scans tail entries (index>=N) and BLANKS any whose blog URL (locale/scheme/trailing-slash-normalized) OR title matches a refreshed post. Guarded by verify_deck Check 6 (blog_coverage) which now also FAILs on any repeated blog entry text.

Changelog highlights are now extracted DETERMINISTICALLY by scripts/fetch_changelogs.py (Phase 1), not the deck-data agent. It resolves each entry's changelog_url to its raw.githubusercontent.com form, fetches each distinct file once, slices the '## <version>' section, and picks ONE bullet by category priority (FEATURES>ENHANCEMENTS>SECURITY>CHANGES>BUG FIXES), stripping PR refs/markdown to a one-line sentence. Stores 'highlight' + (on latest) 'changelog_excerpt'. The agent only LIGHTLY polishes wording from the local excerpt — it must NOT web_fetch changelogs. Cut deck-data web I/O massively.

Terraform Enterprise releases are now fetched DETERMINISTICALLY by scripts/fetch_tfe_releases.py (Phase 1). The releases page is a Next.js doc: parse __NEXT_DATA__ and match each release row's anchor '/terraform/enterprise/releases/<year>/v<version>' (robust). Calendar versions vYYYYMM-N yield month/year directly. FRESHNESS GUARD is deterministic: read the ORIGINAL deck slide8's max 'Terraform Enterprise vX (YYYY-MM-DD)' date and if the newest fetched release date <= that, set recent=[]/latest=null/status='stale_source' (never downgrade). The agent no longer web_fetches the page or digs git history.

Repointing a run's hyperlink via add_rel/relink_run mints a fresh rId and leaves the run's PREVIOUS hyperlink rel dangling in the .rels (reviewer found slide7 rId11 -> an old v1.16.0-alpha tag). All three deterministic editors now call pptx_edit.prune_orphan_hyperlinks(slide_dom, rels_dom) before writing: it removes ONLY relationships of the hyperlink Type whose Id is referenced by no element (r:id/r:embed/r:link) — so implicit/internal rels (slideLayout, image, notesSlide) are never touched. verify_deck also treats a stale/None product latest as satisfied (slide correctly left unchanged).

Featured/webinar event slides retain a non-visible <a:hlinkClick> inside <a:endParaRPr> after refresh (slide 20 endParaRPr -> old kpnhpdmb, slide 22 -> automationday-jun11-Paris). edit_event_slides.py repoints the visible Register Here run but not the paragraph-end link, so link audits chase phantom targets. Clear or repoint endParaRPr hlinks too (same fix already applied to edit_release_slides.py). Harmless to readers (no glyphs) but flag in audits.

ROOT CAUSE of the silent review/learning failure (run 1150): verify_deck's checks encoded the WRONG defaults, so a deck with empty webinar slots, a blanked blog box, and a skipped same-month release was OVERALL PASS — the AI reviewer faithfully reported it as correct, and the learning loop (which only records FLAGGED defects) learned nothing. Fix = make the verifier's defaults match the hand-authored standard: added Check 8 (no_empty_box) and Check 9 (release_gap) as hard FAILs. Lesson: the verifier is the source of truth for 'correct'; if it tolerates a defect, the whole review+learning loop is blind to it. Encode every human-stated standard as a deterministic gate, not just agent prose.

Webinar slides 10/14 must NEVER show an empty slot. The hand-authored deck always filled every slot, backfilling with certification/cross-product/regional webinars (and, when needed, featured events). fetch_events.py now keeps a full pool: webinars.other[] holds untagged/cert/cross-product webinars (previously DROPPED), and slots carry products[]/type. edit_event_slides.py allocates GLOBALLY: each slide takes its own product's webinars first, then backfills remaining slots from (other-bucket + other-product webinars + featured NOT already on 18-22), soonest-first, relabeling the slot's '| WEBINAR |' segment to the event's type (e.g. '| CONFERENCE |'). Featured shown on 18-22 are reserved/excluded so nothing appears twice. Guarded by verify_deck Check 8 (no empty slot on a VISIBLE webinar slide).

Same-month release patches must NOT be dropped as historical. Old editor REPLACED col3's top entry on a same-month update, overwriting vault 2.0.2 with 2.0.3 (slide 11), and could not shift slide 12's multi-entry columns at all. Fixes: fetch_releases.py adds products.

.month_window (all same major.minor releases in the API window) and fetch_changelogs.py gives each a highlight; edit_release_slides.py now (a) ADDS latest ABOVE an existing distinct stable col3 entry instead of replacing it, (b) has a generalized shift_new_month that handles ANY per-column entry counts by moving entire entry paragraph-groups (style/links intact) and builds the new month column from ALL that month's month_window releases, and (c) runs ensure_month_complete to splice in any missing same-month patch. Result: slides 11 AND 12 show 2.0.3 AND 2.0.2. Guarded by verify_deck Check 9 (release_gap).

Blog slides 9/13 now use INSERT-AND-SHIFT, not overwrite-top-N+blank. The old approach overwrote the top entries (losing curated posts) and BLANKED a tail entry that duplicated a refreshed post -> an empty box (slide 13). SUPERSEDES the earlier 'de-dup by blanking the tail' rule. New edit_blog_slides.py: reads all 8 existing entries, computes which blogs.json posts are genuinely new (not already shown), inserts those at the TOP, shifts every existing entry DOWN one, lets the oldest fall off the bottom — all 8 boxes stay filled, nothing overwritten or duplicated, no empty box. No-op (byte-stable) when there are no new posts. verify_deck Check 6 (blog_coverage) rewritten to insert-and-shift semantics (new posts at top, no fixed top-N demand) and Check 8 fails on any blanked box vs the original's entry count.

Completeness is a property of the WHOLE displayed release window, not just the current month. The skipped-patch you flagged (HCP Terraform missing a May .x patch / the 1.15.5 mislabel cascade) lived in a HISTORICAL column (May, col2), but Check 9 and the editor's completeness pass were scoped to the LATEST month only — so a historical gap could ship. Fixes: (a) edit_release_slides.ensure_window_complete now runs ensure_month_complete for EVERY month present in month_window, and runs UNCONDITIONALLY on non-fallback slides (even when 'latest already present; no shift needed'), so a historical gap with no new release is still repaired; (b) verify_deck Check 9 audits every DISPLAYED month column (a month entirely absent has scrolled off the rolling window -> skipped; a partial month -> FAIL). Proven: synthesizing a missing May 1.15.4 makes Check 9 FAIL, and the editor splices it back to 9/9 PASS.

Slide 14 (vault webinars): all 4 slots must be filled; if fewer than 4 vault webinars exist, backfill remaining slots from featured events NOT already on slides 18-22, soonest-first. Never leave a slot blank.

Webinar slide backfill must be soonest-first: sort all candidate backfill events by date ascending and pick the earliest ones not already on slides 18-22. Never skip over nearer-date events to pick a later one.
Webinar slide slot order must be soonest-upcoming first (ascending date). Fill slot 1 with the nearest event, slot 2 with the next, etc.

Featured event slides (18-22): the date-prefix run (e.g. 'Event | June 24 | ') must have its hlinkClick repointed to the same URL as Register Here, not a stale URL from a previous slide assignment. Add a fresh rel for the event URL and apply it to both the date-prefix run and the Register Here run.

Featured event photos: prefer EACH event's OWN decluttered per-city leadspace hero (clean title + brand gradient; declutter hides the Register button/forms/contact e-mails/breadcrumbs via shadow-DOM visibility:hidden so height is preserved for a cover-crop). The matching HashiCorp series hero is only a FALLBACK for events whose page has no leadspace (e.g. a hands-on lab). Always reject registration-page screenshots with visible buttons/forms/contact e-mails/large blank-white areas.

Blog tail entries (carry-over rows below the top-N refresh) must have their 'See here' hyperlinks validated against their displayed title — a URL that doesn't match the post title is a FAIL. edit_blog_slides.py (or verify_deck) should cross-check each non-recent entry's rId target URL against a canonical slug derived from the title; or, when a tail entry is first written, its URL must be verified as reachable and title-matched before being stored.

Featured event city/location photos must match the event's city. A London event slide must show a London landmark; Amsterdam event shows Amsterdam; Hanoi shows Hanoi or the ARSE hero only. Verify: for each featured slide, the city photo's image file used should have been fetched/sourced for that city. Wrong-city photos (e.g. Amsterdam canal on London slide) are a FAIL. When no verified city photo is available, use the ARSE series hero alone rather than a mismatched stock photo.

Vault Enterprise (slide 11) carry-over release entries must use the clean one-line highlight from data/releases.json, not a raw changelog excerpt. When a same-month patch is added above an existing entry (per the shift rule), the EXISTING entry's highlight must also be validated: if it does not match the data highlight for that version, rewrite it from the data. A verbose multi-sentence description with 'Breaking change:' lines is a sign of raw changelog copy-paste.

Webinar-slot backfill must reserve in-person featured events by event IDENTITY (title+date), never by raw url. Several distinct featured events share a generic landing-page url (AWS Summit DC/Mexico City/Zurich all link to aws.amazon.com/events/summits/); a url-keyed reservation drops the non-reserved AWS Summits from the backfill pool and leaves later webinar slides (e.g. slide 14 Vault) with empty boxes -> verify_deck no_empty_box FAIL. Fixed in scripts/edit_event_slides.py allocate_webinars (reserved_featured_ids).

Featured-event hero (slides 18-22) must be the event CITY photo (config/city-photos.yaml -> bundled deck media or a freely-licensed file in assets/city-photos/), keyed by events.json 'location'. NEVER use the IBM/HashiCorp leadspace or series webpage screenshot as the hero: it duplicated the slide's own Title/date/description text, carried a stray horizontal divider line, and cover-cropped through the middle (cut the sparkle icons off the top and the paragraph off the bottom on slide 19; clipped the title on slide 21). edit_event_slides.py resolves the city photo and removes every other extra picture so each slide shows ONE clean city hero; verify_deck.photo_consistency hashes the embedded hero against the resolved city photo.

Every featured hero photo (slides 18-22) must use IDENTICAL rounded corners (a:prstGeom roundRect adj 1178). The template leaves slide 18's hero a plain rect; edit_event_slides.set_round_corners forces roundRect on every swapped hero so all five match.

Every featured slide (18-22) carries the HashiCorp/IBM brand logo overlay in the bottom-left of the hero: the 'HashiCorp / An IBM Company' lockup with GRADIENT-FILLED letters (brand blue->purple->pink->orange, same as the 'Featured/In Person Events' divider), NOT a solid color and NOT on a background chip. Asset assets/brand/hashicorp-ibm-gradient.png (regen via scripts/gen_brand_logo.py); placed by edit_event_slides.place_brand_logo; enforced by verify_deck brand_logo check.

Featured-event description_points must be FULL explanatory sentences (~150-200 chars / ~25-45 words each, ~400-600 chars total across 2-3 points), matching the deck's original hand-authored event blurbs - NOT terse 3-8 word fragments. deck-data MUST web_fetch the event page and ground every claim; never invent speakers/agendas to pad length.

Brand logo legibility over photos uses a SOFT DARK GLOW (centered blurred dark halo behind the gradient letters), NOT a white/black border/outline (outlines look sticker-ish on a gradient logo). Tuned in scripts/gen_brand_logo.py (stacked GaussianBlur halo); placement BRAND_LOGO_WIDTH_FRAC/INSET_FRAC in edit_event_slides.py.

All five featured hero photos (18-22) must share ONE canonical geometry (CANON_HERO: x=43 y=154 w=473 h=346 px). The template positions them slightly differently (e.g. slide 19 x=33 vs 43; heights 336-353); edit_featured_slide forces _set_xfrm(hero, CANON_HERO) on every hero so it's a consistent pattern.

Featured description_points: FIRM, confident, customer-facing sentences (active voice, specific, NOT robotic/generic AI phrasing), CONCISE 2-3 points ~60-110 chars each / ~200-340 total so they fit beside the photo at full size without overflowing the image height. fill_description sets a:normAutofit with a length-based fontScale (100% <=360 chars) as an overflow safety, and strips a:buNone so every point keeps a bullet (slide 22's p0 shipped buNone).

Featured-event description text (slides 18-22) must be UNIFORM: 14pt (sz 1400, matching slide 18; some templates ship 12pt), vertically centered (bodyPr anchor=ctr), and bullets consistent - strip any marL/indent override on a paragraph (slide 22's p0 shipped marL=0 indent=0 which collapsed its bullet hang). edit_event_slides._uniform_description applies this; style_check only guards colors/typeface, not size, so 14pt is allowed.

Event/blog/release prose must NOT use em dashes or en dashes (—/–) or AI-tell words (leverage, seamless, delve, robust, 'in today's') - they read as AI-generated. Use plain punctuation (commas/periods/colons). deck-data instructions enforce this; reword any dash the agent emits.

Webinar slides (10, 14) must contain ONLY real webinars. Never backfill empty slots with conferences or featured/in-person events. If a product has fewer webinars than slots, leave the extra slots empty (the verify gate now allows empty webinar slots). Hide the slide only if zero webinars exist.
Featured-event slides should surface ALL upcoming/future events from today onward (the fetcher scrolls the events page to the bottom), not just the first page.

Events and webinars are REGION-SCOPED to config/sources.yaml events.scope_regions (default [EMEA, MENA]). Only place events/webinars whose location is in scope; online webinars with no location are kept. Scope is applied identically in fetch_events, edit_event_slides and verify_deck via lib/regions.scope_events. Unknown regions are kept (never silently dropped).

Terraform Enterprise releases are NOT on the public releases API (api.releases.hashicorp.com has no terraform-enterprise product; 'terraform' there is the Community Edition / 1.x CLI). TFE ships under the new semver scheme on per-series pages (developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/enterprise/releases/<N.M>.x, e.g. 2.0.x) whose notes list each version + date + bullets. fetch_tfe_releases.py reads the newest series page (not the old /<year>/vYYYYMM-N calendar links) and extracts version, real date, and a one-line highlight. Slide 8 hyperlinks must point to the TFE release-notes URL (.../<N.M>.x#a-b-c), NOT a github.com/hashicorp/terraform tag (no such tag exists for 2.x). New TFE entries keep the 'Terraform Enterprise vX (date)' prefix.

Webinar/event PRODUCT tagging must be BADGE-driven, for ALL products. Each events-page card shows one coloured product badge per product (svg class 'flight-icon--color' with a 'Terraform' label); fetch_events.render_cards extracts those into card['products'] and parse_card uses them as authoritative. NEVER keyword-match the title to a product (that over-tagged, e.g. a 'policy'/'security' title onto Vault). A webinar is bucketed into every product it is badged with (Terraform-only -> Terraform slide only; Boundary+Vault -> Vault). The only title fallback is an exact product-name word, used solely when a card has no badge at all; otherwise it goes to the cross-product 'other' pool.

run.sh must be Bash 3.2-safe (macOS system bash): expand possibly-empty arrays as ${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"} instead of "${arr[@]}", which throws 'unbound variable' under set -u in Bash 3.2 (e.g. COPY_ARGS at Phase 2, model_args in run_copilot).

Config slide-map 'n' values are deck POSITIONS and can drift when the deck gains/reorders slides. This JUNE 2026 deck inserted an extra date-based 'HCP Terraform Upgrades' slide at position 9, shifting every automatable slide >=9 by +1 (blogs 9->10/13->14, webinars 10->11/14->15, Vault Ent 11->12, HCP Vault 12->13) while the semver 'Terraform Core - GitHub Releases' (7) and TFE (8) stayed. Featured events are the 4 real event slides 19-22 (slide 18 'Featured/In Person Events' is a section INTRO, never edited). Symptom: editors hide/edit the WRONG files (blogs slides 10/14 got show=0, Vault releases unchecked, London event dropped onto the intro). Fix: realign every slide-map 'n' to the actual deck file number (map by title/content, verify with presentation.xml order).

HCP release slides (variant: hcp, e.g. HCP Vault slide 13, HCP Terraform) are DATE-based broad-rollout slides ('HCP Vault 2.0 rolling out', dated) with NO patch-semver tokens. verify_deck release_columns must validate their currency by the rightmost column's MONTH header == latest month_label, not by requiring the latest patch version string (which never appears). edit_release_slides flags them as fallback because its version-column logic can't see date entries; that's fine — if col3's month is current, leave the slide unchanged.

verify_deck blog_coverage freshness is now URL-aware: a post is 'already present' (not a missing fresh insert) if its title OR its normalized hyperlink URL (ignore scheme, locale '/en/', trailing slash) is on the original slide. This matches edit_blog_slides' own URL-based dedup and prevents a false 'new post not placed' when the deck transcribed a title slightly differently (e.g. 'What is new with Terraform + Ansible' vs the canonical 'What's new...') while linking the same blog.

Pre-existing hand-authored bullet glyph fonts in the source deck (e.g. buFont typeface='Arial,Sans-Serif' on the HCP Vault slide) are legitimate; add them to palette.json fonts.fallback so the style guard doesn't flag a value the deck already shipped with. The featured section-intro slide (18) carries a near-brand vault hex (F9B570 ~ F9B571) but is out of edit scope, so it's no longer style-checked once it's excluded from slide-map.

Featured hero reuse bug: a per-city leadspace capture that bakes in a SPECIFIC event's title/date (e.g. city-london.png IS the 'HashiCorp Agentic Runtime Security Exchange - London / June 25, 2026' leadspace) must NOT be reused as a generic city hero for a DIFFERENT event that merely shares the city/country. Slide 21 (CISO UK, July 1) was given city-london.png, so its hero displays the London Agentic event's title and date - contradicting the slide's own CISO UK / July 1 text. edit_event_slides.py resolves featured photos by location (UK->London) and treated the London event's own leadspace as a reusable city asset. Per slide-map, an unrelated event whose page has no leadspace and whose title matches no SERIES hero must KEEP ITS EXISTING photo (or use a text-free city skyline), never borrow another event's branded leadspace. Only reuse a leadspace capture for the exact event it was captured from (match by event url/title, not just city).

Featured-event city photos must be FREELY-LICENSED FILE assets (assets/city-photos/*.jpg), never config/city-photos.yaml source:bundled by media index (image46.png). Bundled-by-index is deck-fragile: a different source deck can place an EVENT LEADSPACE at that index (this JUNE deck's image46/48 are the 'Agentic Runtime Security Exchange - London/Amsterdam' leadspaces with the event title+venue+date baked in), so CISO UK (UK->London) showed the wrong event's branding. London=Tower Bridge, Amsterdam=Damrak (both CC BY-SA 4.0, see CREDITS). Also the repo will go public, so don't commit the deck's unknown-license stock images.

Featured-event location must be extracted title-aware via lib.regions.place_in (used by fetch_events._featured), not only the trailing '- City' dash pattern. Titles like 'AWS Summit Zurich' (->Zurich) and 'CISO UK' (->UK) carry the place without a dash; without this their location was empty and the city-photo resolver placed no hero (the deck-data agent used to backfill it, but the gate skips agents when the deterministic deck already passes).

Terraform now has THREE release slides in this deck: 'Terraform Core - GitHub Releases' (pos 7, CE/version-based, products.terraform, variant core), 'Terraform Enterprise Upgrades' (pos 8, terraform-enterprise/TFE), and 'HCP Terraform Upgrades' (pos 9, DATE-based, variant hcp - editor flags fallback, verify checks col3 month vs products.terraform.latest). slide-map n: are POSITIONS; remap by title via presentation.xml order when the deck reorders.

Webinar slot descriptions are MANDATORY: edit_event_slides.fill_webinar_slot must (1) write the deck-data description when present, (2) else PRESERVE the source slide's existing hand-authored blurb (never blank it), (3) else synthesize a product-aware fallback. verify_deck now FAILs no_empty_box if any FILLED webinar slot has an empty description.

Webinar-slot flags are region-aware: US flag (assets/flags/us.png) for US/AMERICAS events, Union Jack for UK/European/English. An English webinar must NEVER flip the deck author's existing US-vs-UK flag (we can't tell US from UK English by title) - set_slot_flag preserves an existing en/us flag and only sets us when the event resolves to AMERICAS. _DESCR_LANG maps 'usa'/'united states' -> us, 'union jack'/'united kingdom' -> en.

Recent-blog slides must be DATE-ORDERED: edit_blog_slides sorts the merged (fresh+existing) entries newest-first before truncating to 8, because the source deck's blog boxes are not always chronological - a plain position shift dropped a RECENT post (June 9 'zero trust') off the bottom while keeping older ones. blogs recent_count raised 3->6 so enough candidates are considered.

Featured-event description box must be 14pt + VERTICALLY CENTERED (bodyPr anchor=ctr) even when there are no deck-data description_points and the source blurb is preserved - apply _uniform_description in that branch too, else slides without points (CISO UK, Zurich) render top-anchored unlike 19/20.

releases.stable_only is now WIRED in fetch_releases (was dead config). Keep terraform stable_only:true: a daily 1.16.0-alphaYYYYMMDD is a preview of the next minor and is typically superseded the SAME day by the latest stable patch (1.15.7 shipped 16:47 vs alpha 14:08), so the stable patch is the real latest; enabling prereleases also pollutes month_window with rc/beta and breaks release_gap.

Featured-event section AUTO-GROWS with no cap: when upcoming in-scope events > template featured slides, edit_event_slides duplicates the last featured slide (via lib.pptx_edit.duplicate_slide_after, which reuses the pptx skill add_slide.py + splices the <p:sldId> right after the section) so EVERY upcoming event gets a slide. Deck count may GROW but never shrink; verify_deck integrity now allows count>=original. Date-sorting/auto-grow reassign events to slots, so a featured slide keeps its hand-authored blurb ONLY when the event's city matches the slot's existing title (_same_event), else a synthesized fallback (_fallback_featured_points) is written - never inherit a template/other event's description.

Webinar slot descriptions must be ONE concise sentence (<=155 chars) — edit_event_slides._one_sentence trims them. The slot box is small (~265x176px, 6.5pt, noAutofit) and is sized for a single sentence (deck-data writes one); the source deck ships long multi-sentence blurbs (207-248 chars) that overflow when preserved verbatim. Applies to deck-data, preserved-source, and fallback descriptions alike.

Featured-event hero photos must be freely-licensed, deck-independent city skylines under assets/city-photos/ (config/city-photos.yaml, source: file) — never bundled-by-media-index (deck-fragile: a different deck can carry an event leadspace at the same image index). Coverage now includes Paris, Berlin, Madrid, Munich, Dublin, Milan and Dubai plus aliases (Munchen->munich, Milano->milan, Ireland->dublin, UAE->dubai). Add new event cities here (prefer CC0/PD) and the slide picks them up with no code change.

verify_deck must cover AUTO-GROWN featured slides, not just the static slide-map slots. featured_slide_ns() enumerates featured slide FILE numbers from the event-edit-report (featured entries lack a webinar 'slots' key), with a structural fallback (contiguous brand-logo'd slides after the last static featured slide in display order). The event-coverage, photo-consistency and brand-logo checks all iterate this list, and event-coverage FAILS when there are more in-scope featured events than featured slides (auto-grow shortfall).

Before trusting slide-map.yaml's hardcoded featured-event slide numbers, verify each listed slide actually has a 'Register Here' hyperlink + Title 1 + Content Placeholder (the real event-card template) — a monthly deck edition may ship with FEWER event-card templates than a prior edition (e.g. only 1 real slot instead of 4), with the extra listed numbers being a section divider and/or unrelated internal slides (Engagement Status, Follow Up Items). Treating those as event slots corrupts the deck: it hides the real template and wrongly hides out-of-scope slides. Fix by updating the config's featured 'n' list to only the slide(s) with the real template pattern, then restore any wrongly-hidden out-of-scope slides.

Date-keyed release reconcile (edit_release_slides.reconcile) must not blindly overwrite a column entry's version just because releases.json's by_date index disagrees — by_date collapses to ONE version per calendar date, but HashiCorp sometimes ships an alpha/pre-release (e.g. vX.(Y+1).0-alpha) on the SAME calendar date as an unrelated stable patch (e.g. vX.Y.Z). Blindly substituting the version number (VERSION_RE.sub) while leaving the '- alpha'/'Pre-release' framing text intact produces a duplicate entry: the same stable version appears twice in one column (once correctly labeled, once mislabeled as an alpha pre-release), contradicting releases.json's is_prerelease=false. Before reconciling, check whether the entry's OWN existing text already reads as a pre-release/alpha (PRERELEASE_RE) for a DIFFERENT minor/major line than by_date's version; if so, treat it as a distinct legitimate release on that date and leave it untouched (or flag for agent review) rather than merging it into the stable entry.

Webinar-slot flags must be detected for BOTH geometries: a slot's language flag may be a circular ellipse (Union Jack/German the deck ships) OR a rect image whose alt-text names a country (e.g. 'Italy flag - free Icon PNG, SVG'). edit_event_slides.flag_pics now includes rect flags identified via _descr_lang(descr); and flag_for_slot never steals a flag that sits inside another slot's box (other_boxes guard). Before the fix the Vault webinars slide showed TWO Italian flags: the Italian webinar's own flag was a rect (invisible to the ellipse-only detector), so it grabbed the neighbouring English slot's ellipse flag and set it Italian, leaving the English slot mislabeled.

Featured / in-person event slides must show ONLY the product logos the event actually covers. The top band carries small HashiCorp product icons (this deck: Vault=image34.png, Terraform=image39.svg via svgBlip); a reassigned/duplicated event must not keep the template's icon for a product it isn't about. edit_event_slides.match_product_icons classifies each small top-band picture by EXACT content-hash against bundled assets/product-icons/<product>.<ext> (byte-identical copies of the deck's own logo media) and removes the logo of any product not in events.json 'products', keeping the rest; partner logos (AWS) and the HashiCorp/IBM brand lockup are left untouched. Exact-hash (not colour) is used deliberately: AWS's orange swoosh (hue ~36) is too close to Vault gold (~47) for safe colour matching. No-op when the event has no product tags (never strip icons we can't validate). Orphan image rels are pruned so the unused logo media is dropped at pack time.
